verdict: American Express posted record revenue of $20.1B (+9%) on strong card spending, and net income rose 28% to $3.7B — EPS of $5.42 included a $982M gain from selling its stake in Global Business Travel.

kpis.label: Revenue (net of interest expense)
kpis.note: A record, +9% vs a year ago

segments.name: U.S. Consumer Services
segments.note: Cards for U.S. consumers — Millennial and Gen-Z members are the largest and fastest-growing group. Segment revenue as reported was $9,840M; shown net of $95M of corporate and intersegment items so the parts sum to the company total.

segments.name: Commercial Services
segments.note: Cards and payments for businesses, from small firms to large corporates.

segments.name: International Card Services
segments.note: Consumer and small-business cards outside the U.S. — Amex's fastest-growing segment, with billed business up 11%.

segments.name: Global Merchant & Network Services
segments.note: Fees from merchants that accept Amex and from partners that issue cards on its network.

opex.name: Card Member rewards
opex.note: Points, cash back and partner rewards — the price of premium cardholders' spending, up 10% with billed business.

opex.name: Card Member services
opex.note: Travel and lifestyle benefits — up 36% after last year's U.S. Platinum refresh added richer perks.

opex.name: Business development
opex.note: Payments to partners, including co-brand and network partners.

opex.name: Other, net
opex.note: Data processing ($858M), professional services ($675M) and other costs ($764M), reduced by the $982M GBTG gain.

takeaways.title: Record revenue of $20.1B
takeaways.text: Card spending (billed business) rose 8% to $454B, discount revenue grew 8%, and card fees jumped 16% after the Platinum refresh.

takeaways.title: A one-off gain flattered EPS
takeaways.text: Selling its ~30% stake in Global Business Travel Group added a $982M pre-tax gain ($1.11 a share); part was reinvested via a $336M restructuring charge. Adjusted EPS of $4.68 strips both out.

takeaways.title: Credit costs fell
takeaways.text: Provisions for credit losses dropped 23% to $985M on a reserve release, with write-off and delinquency rates stable — Amex's premium customers kept paying.

oneTimers: GAAP results include a $982M pre-tax gain on the sale of Amex's equity stake in Global Business Travel Group (closed Sep 29, 2026) and a $336M restructuring charge; adjusted EPS of $4.68 excludes both.
footerNote: Bank model: revenue is total revenues net of interest expense, and provisions for credit losses are shown as the direct cost, following the format used for other banks on this site. Operating income here equals pre-tax income; there is no separate non-operating line in Amex's presentation.
